hook: SCP-2639 opens as a dry report about a cube of space where armored figures appear and vanish, then becomes something else through a long run of chat logs. Read the logs at your own pace; much of the effect comes from typos, emoticons and the silences between messages.
whyItMatters: Written by The Great Hippo, it turns a gamer-culture premise into a story about guilt and responsibility. Its ending forms a Mobile Task Force, which ties the article into later files that list that unit as assisting in containment. Even the reclassification from Keter to Euclid is part of the story rather than a footnote.
thingsToNotice: The description and the incident database plant the reveal before the chat confirms it, and the 'Ammo Pack' item that appears only when someone dies is the detail to keep in mind. The friends' easy banter at the start makes the turn harder to read, because the reader understands what the game has been before they do. The researcher's long one-sided check-ins show the Foundation at its most humane, and his admission that he cannot truly grasp their pain is the emotional center. The breach scene and the final agreement turn the trio's skill into a kind of atonement, bound by a strict rule they set for themselves.

related.note: Lists the task force formed in this article among its assisting units.
An early-series game show anomaly where play carries real stakes.
